result:
Verdict: **APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES**. The backlog is dependency-closed with no cycles, user steering and effort accounting have a single explicit owner in CORE-10 that precedes recovery and native consumers, local and remote proofs are staged incrementally, startup recovery is layered across CORE-05, CORE-06, CORE-08, CORE-09, OPS-02 and OPS-06, and no ticket weakens an accepted requirement. Five actionable gaps follow; none is a rejection-level defect.

## Substantive gaps and repairs

**1. Unowned file creators.** NATIVE-01 says "extend the qualified" `tests/native/profile.test.ts`, but no ticket creates that file. CORE-03 only "qualifies narrow bindings in" the two adapter entry files and the admitted-view file, which NATIVE-01, NATIVE-03 and NATIVE-04 later "extend the qualified" versions of, so creation is implied but never stated. OPS-03 lists the input-bundle and remote-operations modules without a verb. The campaign contract says proposed files exist only if a predecessor created them, so an implementing seat will hit an ambiguity at plan review.
Repair: change CORE-03 to "create" the two adapter index files and the admitted-view boundary as narrow qualification bindings. Change NATIVE-01 to "create" the profile test fixture. Change OPS-03 to "create" the input-bundle and remote-operations modules and "extend" capture and the adapter registrations.

**2. Remote work is not bound to the CORE-10 effort scope or to individually identified steering barriers.** CORE-10 requires every descendant, retry and successor to charge one accounting scope, with reservations before dispatch and unknown usage retained. OPS-03 retains remote model and effort observations and OPS-04 persists a GPU execution budget, but neither states that a remote attempt carries the local accounting scope identity, that a reservation is made before submit, or that usage captured offline settles exactly once on collect or replay. OPS-03 mentions "pending cancel/scope barriers" on reconnect, but pause and revision barriers are not named with their individual identities, so the CORE-10 rule that resume resolves only named barriers is not carried remotely.
Repair: add to OPS-03 acceptance: the durable launch intent records the accounting scope identity, reservation before submit, once-only settlement of remote usage through collect and replay, and unknown remote usage retained. Add to OPS-04: lease renewal and final dispatch validate the current set of named barriers, and reconnect delivers pause, cancel and revision barriers by identity, distinct from the GPU budget which is a separate limit.

**3. Non-initial schema migration has no explicit owner.** CORE-05 makes non-initial migration unavailable until CORE-09's marker machinery exists. CORE-09 explicitly covers only marker visibility for an interrupted migration, not applying one. NATIVE-09 and NATIVE-11 each add "the next versioned migration", which is fine under sequential integration but only reaches fresh scratch stores. OPS-05 owns the maintenance module and mentions schemas, but never says it applies pending migrations to an existing instance under the external marker with quiescence, verified backup and exclusive ownership, or that an old runtime rejects a migrated store.
Repair: add to OPS-05 an explicit bullet owning guarded non-initial migration through the external maintenance marker, with crash injection before and after application and an old-runtime refusal case in the update fixture. Add one sentence to NATIVE-09 and NATIVE-11 stating their migrations apply only through explicit creation until OPS-05 lands.

**4. OPS-04 conflates the mechanical offline and queue policy with the live S4 remote proof, and the whole S5 chain hangs off it.** The mechanical policy needs only OPS-02 and OPS-03. The live remote native and GPU proof needs NATIVE-13, which transitively requires every S3 asset ticket. Blocking the policy code on NATIVE-07, NATIVE-08 and NATIVE-12 is not a capability prerequisite, and it makes OPS-05, OPS-06 and OPS-07 wait on asset repairs they do not use. It also puts one live provider and GPU obligation inside a ticket whose focused population is mechanical, which blurs the "separately declared bounded plan" rule.
Repair: either split the live proof into its own S4 ticket blocked by OPS-04 and NATIVE-13, with OPS-05 through OPS-07 blocked by the mechanical OPS-04 only, or keep one ticket but state that only the remote complete-slice run waits for NATIVE-13 and that S5 tickets depend on the mechanical population. Either way, record the live proof as a distinct milestone with its own readiness state.

**5. Mandatory verify-group registration is deferred to OPS-10.** CORE-01 creates the fixed registry and requires unknown or unbuilt groups to report unavailable. NATIVE-05, NATIVE-06, NATIVE-08 and NATIVE-12 say they register their case subgroups, but NATIVE-02 does not say it registers `coordination` as a mandatory execution population, even though the delivery workflow requires that. NATIVE-13 extends the registry for the local slice, but store, execution and complete-slice group composition is only fully assembled in OPS-10. Until then the recipient launcher cannot report which mandatory populations are incomplete, which is the truthful-unavailable behaviour the registry exists for.
Repair: require every ticket that creates a fixture to add its registry entry with declared case count and an explicit unavailable or incomplete status until its group closes. Add that sentence to NATIVE-02, CORE-05, CORE-07, CORE-08, CORE-09, OPS-02, OPS-03, OPS-04, OPS-06 and OPS-07. OPS-10 then verifies completeness rather than performing first registration.

**Minor, not blocking:** OPS-05, OPS-06 and OPS-07 rely on the boilerplate both-host clause instead of naming which cases run on Mac as controller, on Linux as runner, and which are Linux-only service-lifetime cases. OPS-02's "on both hosts" is ambiguous for a Mac-to-Linux transport. One clarifying sentence each would help the plan reviewer.

## Coverage checks that passed

- Steering and accounting: CORE-10 sits after CORE-07 and before CORE-08; NATIVE-02, NATIVE-03 and NATIVE-04 bind children and native ingress; CORE-08 repeats cases through crashes; NATIVE-13 includes reset-allowance and pause races.
- Incremental proof: local path CORE-07, CORE-10, CORE-08, CORE-09, NATIVE-13; remote path OPS-02, OPS-03, OPS-04; product proof OPS-09, OPS-10; empirical use OPS-11 correctly excluded from S6.
- Both-host evidence: every S1 through S4 ticket names both hosts and same-candidate identity recording.
- Startup recovery: existing-only open, external marker checked at every startup, runner existing-only ledger, no fresh-setup fallback anywhere.
- Publication and readiness: every ticket carries a packet digest and the untracked-source blocker; the campaign contract's publication transaction is consistent with the ticket status text.

## Read limits

I read every supplied source in full: the campaign contract, consolidated plan, delivery workflow, first complete slice, records-and-transitions, first-run ownership document, remote execution contract and curated asset plan. I read all 34 ticket bodies completely. I did not read the ticket backlog JSON, per-file hashes, the step-plan files, README, source inventory, maintenance-remote-tickets, native-profile-and-lead-binding, memory or improvement documents, or any current implementation files. No tools were used and no digest was verified; packet digest validation remains with the separate local validator.
